ln-moonhare.homeland: The dusk-warrens of the Moonlit Vale
ln-moonhare.environment: Perpetual moonlit dusk and silvered meadows
ln-moonhare.culture: Moonhares are the Vale-warren harengon who dance to the lunar tides and carry omens between the moon-courts. Their moon-dances are read as auguries, and a Moonhare courier is trusted to carry a secret as faithfully as a message.
ln-moonhare.tradition: The Moon-Dance, timed to lunar tides, where the young dance their First Run's tale before the warren.
ln-moonhare.naming: Given name plus a moon-phase (Lira Waxing-Foot).
hooks: A message you carried has started a Moon Court feud
Your moon-dance omen named you for something you don't understand
One of the Nine Lanterns went out on your watch

ln-stormhare.homeland: The ridge-runs of the Stormreach coast
ln-stormhare.environment: The storm-belt's leading edge and lightning-lit ridges
ln-stormhare.culture: Stormhares run the tempest coast, the fastest couriers alive, who deliver word through storms that ground everyone else. They race the lightning for sport and glory, and a Stormhare's Courier's Word is said to outrun the weather itself.
ln-stormhare.tradition: The Storm-Run, delivering a message across the storm-front without stopping, to earn a courier's charm.
ln-stormhare.appearance: Wind-slicked grey fur, static-marked ears, light storm-cloth.
ln-stormhare.naming: Given name plus a storm-run (Dax Boltfoot).
hooks: A storm-run message you carried could stop or start a war
You outran a storm that has since begun hunting you
The Storm spoke to you mid-run and you cannot forget it

ln-wildhare.homeland: The open ranges at the Wilds' frontier
ln-wildhare.environment: Meadow-frontier, hedgerow country, and forest edges
ln-wildhare.culture: Wildhares are the free-roaming harengon of the open country, scouts and pathfinders who know every trail between the settled lands and the Wilds. They keep no fixed warren, only the road and the season, and their First Run circles farther than any other line's.
ln-wildhare.tradition: The First Run, a solo journey between two distant warrens, longest among the Wildhares.
ln-wildhare.appearance: Brown-and-tan fur, trail-worn leathers, foraged charms.
ln-wildhare.naming: Given name plus a trail-name (Bram Longtrail).
ln-wildhare.landmark: The frontier trails of the Wilds' edge
hooks: A trail you scout leads somewhere that was not there before
Your First Run route now passes through the Hunt's range
You are the first Wildhare to try to settle down

ln-duskhare.homeland: The shadow-border warrens near the Vale
ln-duskhare.environment: Twilight border-country between Vale and Shadowlands
ln-duskhare.culture: Duskhares keep the quiet, stranger faiths of the shadow-border, harengon who carry messages where the light thins and few couriers will go. They move unseen through the dusk and know the safe paths across the shadow-border better than anyone alive.
ln-duskhare.tradition: The Dusk-Crossing, a rite of carrying a message across the shadow-border and back by moonlight alone.
ln-duskhare.appearance: Dusk-grey fur, shadow-marked ears, muffling dark wraps.
ln-duskhare.naming: Given name plus a dusk-omen (Vesh Greywhisper).
hooks: A Night Court message you carry has a deadline you can't meet
The shadow-border is advancing across your safe paths
The Unlit tried to hire you and now want you silenced

ln-swiftfoot.homeland: The courier-roads and cities of the Crownlands
ln-swiftfoot.environment: City streets and the great trade-roads
ln-swiftfoot.culture: Swiftfoot harengon are the city-couriers and road-runners of the Crownlands, the fastest legs in any market or guild-hall. They keep the Courier's Word as sacred law, and a Swiftfoot who breaks a delivery is shunned by every warren.
ln-swiftfoot.tradition: The Courier's Word, an unbreakable vow to deliver a message, taught before a Swiftfoot can run for hire.
ln-swiftfoot.naming: Given name plus a route (Pip of the Nine Wards).
ln-swiftfoot.landmark: The great trade-crossroads of the Crownlands
hooks: A Courier's Word binds you to deliver to someone now dead
A message you carried has toppled a guild
You witnessed something on a run that powerful people want buried

ln-direwolf.homeland: The deep-wood ranges of the Emerald Wilds
ln-direwolf.culture: Direwolf packs are the great hunters of the deep Wilds, largest and oldest of the wolfkin, who keep the strictest pack-law. To hunt without need is their deepest taboo, and a Direwolf's pack-name is earned on a solo First Hunt in the deepest wood.
ln-direwolf.tradition: The First Hunt, a solitary hunt in the deep wood to earn one's pack-name.
ln-direwolf.appearance: Massive, grey-furred, scar-marked, bone and claw tokens.
ln-direwolf.naming: Given name plus a hunt-deed (Fenra Deep-Runner).
ln-direwolf.landmark: The Heartwood at the forest's center
hooks: You were cast out and carry a lone-wolf name
Your pack's range-treaty has been broken and blood is owed
The Hunt now runs the same trails as your pack

ln-frostwolf.homeland: The ice-plain ranges of the Frostbound North
ln-frostwolf.environment: Arctic tundra, glacier-fields, and frozen forests
ln-frostwolf.culture: Frostwolf packs run the white north, enduring hunters whose pack-bonds are forged against the killing cold. They share the ice with the frost-clans and bearkin, and their Howl-Moots carry news across distances no runner could cross.
ln-frostwolf.tradition: The Howl-Moot, where packs gather to sing their news, their dead, and their new pack-names into the aurora.
ln-frostwolf.appearance: White-furred, ice-blue eyes, frost-rimed, fur-and-amber tokens.
ln-frostwolf.naming: Given name plus a cold-deed (Skoll Frost-Runner).
ln-frostwolf.landmark: The frozen fjord-ranges of the north
hooks: The Winter Hunt has begun taking from your pack
A Howl-Moot carried word of a pack gone silent
The ice is thinning and your range with it

ln-shadowwolf.homeland: The shadow-border ranges near the Vale
ln-shadowwolf.culture: Shadowwolf packs hold the shadow-border no one else will keep, wolfkin who hunt the things that come out of the dark. Wary neighbors to the night-courts, they move silent through the dusk and are feared by other packs for the company they must keep.
ln-shadowwolf.tradition: The Silent Hunt, a rite of hunting through the shadow-border without a single howl.
ln-shadowwolf.appearance: Shadow-black fur, dusk-grey eyes, muffled dark leathers.
ln-shadowwolf.naming: Given name plus a shadow-deed (Umbra Nightpaw).
hooks: The border-light is failing and the dark is advancing on your range
A night-court noble seeks your pack for a hunt in daylight
Other packs have named yours for consorting with the dark

ln-moonwolf.homeland: The moonlit ranges of the Vale's edge
ln-moonwolf.culture: Moonwolf packs run under the Vale's endless moon, mystics among the wolfkin who read omens in the moon-tides and the hunt. Their howls carry dream-omens, and moon-court nobles seek Moonwolf seers to read the meaning of a night's hunt.
ln-moonwolf.tradition: The Moon-Hunt, a hunt timed to the lunar tide whose course is read for omens.
ln-moonwolf.appearance: Silver-grey fur, moon-pale eyes, lunar-marked, dream-charms.
ln-moonwolf.naming: Given name plus a moon-omen (Sela Moonrunner).
hooks: A moon-hunt omen showed a death you mean to prevent
Your pack's seer has vanished into the Turning Wood
The moon-tides are turning wrong and the omens with them

ln-stormwolf.homeland: The tempest-coast ranges of the Stormreach
ln-stormwolf.culture: Stormwolf packs run the storm-country, wolfkin who hunt through tempests that would ground any other pack and take no penalty in the wind. They believe the Storm hunts alongside them, and their pack-law is as fierce as the weather that shaped it.
ln-stormwolf.tradition: The Storm-Hunt, hunting through a living tempest to prove the pack runs with the Storm.
ln-stormwolf.appearance: Storm-grey fur, static-lit ruffs, wind-worn leathers.
ln-stormwolf.naming: Given name plus a storm-deed (Rax Thunderpaw).
ln-stormwolf.landmark: The Eye, the calm at the storm's center
hooks: The Storm led your hunt to something it wanted found
A rival pack claims your storm-range
The tempest that shelters your pack has begun to fail

ln-greatowl.homeland: The roost-towers of the deep Emerald Wilds
ln-greatowl.culture: Great Owls are the loremaster-owlkin of the deep Wilds, keepers of the Witness-books that record what happens while the world sleeps. Patient and silent, they hold the closest thing to unbroken history, and a Great Owl's testimony can settle a war.
ln-greatowl.tradition: The Long Watch, a solitary vigil marking adulthood, its every observation entered in the roost's Witness-book.
ln-greatowl.naming: Given name plus a watch-name (Aelwyn Nightwatch).
rivals: Those who would burn a Witness-book
ln-greatowl.landmark: The roost-library spires of the deep Wilds
hooks: A page torn from your roost's Witness-book named the Nameless Emperor
Your Long Watch showed something you were not meant to see
Someone is hunting the keepers of the Witness-books

ln-snowowl.homeland: The glacier-roosts of the Frostbound North
ln-snowowl.culture: Snow Owls keep the aurora-vigils of the north, owlkin seers who read the northern lights as ancestor-fire and guard the memory of the dead kings under ice. Silent and still, they watch over the Aurora Vault and warn the holds of what the ice gives up.
ln-snowowl.tradition: The Aurora-Watch, a vigil beneath the northern lights to read the ancestors' will.
ln-snowowl.appearance: Snow-white plumage, pale-gold eyes, frost-quiet robes.
ln-snowowl.naming: Given name plus an aurora-omen (Vela Frostwatch).
hooks: The aurora has changed color over the Vault and only you read the warning
A dead king is thawing and your vigil foresaw it
The ancestor-fire showed a name that should be dead

ln-nightowl.environment: Perpetual dusk and dream-tides of the Vale
ln-nightowl.culture: Night Owls are the dream-wardens of the Vale, owlkin who guard sleepers from the dream-eaters and hunt those who traffic in stolen dreams. They read omens in dreams as others read them in stars, and Silvermere itself answers their watch.
ln-nightowl.tradition: The Dream-Watch, guarding a sleeper through the night to learn the reading of dreams.
ln-nightowl.appearance: Dusk-grey plumage, dark-gold eyes, dream-silk robes.
ln-nightowl.naming: Given name plus a dream-omen (Sable Duskwatch).
hooks: A dream-thief is stealing memories and your ward was the first target
Three sleepers dreamed the same fate and you must learn why
A dream-eater has crossed into the waking Vale

ln-ghostowl.culture: Ghost Owls are the silent watchers of the shadow-border, owlkin so quiet they are said to be half in the dark themselves. They keep vigil over what the shadow hides and carry warnings the living need but fear to hear.
ln-ghostowl.tradition: The Hollow-Watch, a vigil kept in total silence at the edge of the deepest shadow.
ln-ghostowl.appearance: Ash-grey and near-translucent plumage, luminous pale eyes, shadow-silk.
ln-ghostowl.naming: Given name plus a shadow-omen (Wraith Greywatch).
hooks: Your hollow-watch saw the border-light begin to fail
You carry a warning no one wants to believe
The Unlit are hunting the Ghost Owls who watch them

ln-sunowl.homeland: The high dawn-roosts of the Celestial Heights
ln-sunowl.environment: Rarefied luminous heights and dawn-lit spires
ln-sunowl.culture: Sun Owls are the rarest owlkin, dwelling among the seraphim in the Celestial Heights, star-readers who watch the constellations for the Radiant Choir. Where other owlkin watch the dark, Sun Owls watch the light, and they were the first to notice the stars going out.
ln-sunowl.tradition: The Dawn-Watch, a vigil kept through the night to greet and read the first light.
ln-sunowl.appearance: Gold-white plumage, sun-bright eyes, starlight-glass ornaments.
ln-sunowl.naming: Given name plus a star-name (Aurel Dawnwatch).
ln-sunowl.landmark: The Threshold at the edge of the world
hooks: You were first to see the stars over the Threshold going out
The Choir wants your reading of a forbidden prophecy
A Fallen seraph trusts you with a warning the Choir buried

ln-bengal.homeland: The jungle-territories of the deep Wilds
ln-bengal.culture: Bengals are the jungle tigerkin, solitary sovereigns who each rule the ground they stand on and bow to no pack. Their honor-duels settle disputes without war, and a Bengal's guest, once welcomed, is under sacred sanctuary.
ln-bengal.tradition: The Claiming, marking a first territory to earn adulthood, defended by honor-challenge.
ln-bengal.appearance: Ember-orange and black striping, personal sigil-marks, duel-trophies.
ln-bengal.naming: A single proud name plus a territory (Rakh of the Green River).
ln-bengal.landmark: The river-territories of the deep Wilds
hooks: An honor-challenge has followed you across the world
You broke a guest-sanctuary and owe a life-debt
You lost your first territory and wander to reclaim your honor

ln-whitetiger.homeland: The cold heights of the high Ironspine
ln-whitetiger.environment: Snow-capped peaks and high alpine forest
ln-whitetiger.culture: White Tigers withdrew to the cold heights in the Age of Ash, tigerkin of the snow-line who keep the oldest honor-codes in near-isolation. Rarely seen, they descend only to answer a debt or a worthy challenge, and their word is considered unbreakable.
ln-whitetiger.tradition: The Snow-Vigil, a solitary trial in the high cold to prove one is worthy of the old codes.
ln-whitetiger.appearance: White and slate striping, ice-pale eyes, frost-marked sigils.
ln-whitetiger.naming: A single name plus a peak (Sarn of the Silver Peak).
rivals: Those who violate the old codes
hooks: A debt has called you down from the heights for the first time in years
Someone impersonates the White Tiger codes to justify a crime
A worthy challenger has climbed to your snow-line

ln-shadowtiger.culture: Shadow Tigers took to the border in the Blood Wars, solitary hunters who move unseen through the dusk and take contracts the prides would refuse. Feared as assassins, they keep a strict personal honor even in the dark, and a Shadow Tiger's given word is never sold.
ln-shadowtiger.tradition: The Unseen Claiming, marking a territory no one ever sees you patrol.
ln-shadowtiger.appearance: Shadow-black and charcoal striping, dusk-gold eyes, muffled dark wraps.
ln-shadowtiger.naming: A single name plus a shadow-mark (Vael of the Long Dusk).
rivals: Those who break their given word
hooks: A contract you took turns out to serve the Unlit
Your unseen territory has been trespassed by something worse than you
A given word binds you to protect an enemy

ln-stormtiger.homeland: The tempest-coast territories of the Stormreach
ln-stormtiger.culture: Storm Tigers hold the storm-country, tigerkin who claim territory in the tempest itself and hunt through weather that grounds all others. They read the Storm as a rival worthy of respect, and their honor-duels are fought on ridgelines in the teeth of the wind.
ln-stormtiger.tradition: The Storm-Claiming, marking a territory a challenger must reach through a living tempest.
ln-stormtiger.appearance: Storm-grey and violet striping, static-lit eyes, storm-glass sigils.
ln-stormtiger.naming: A single name plus a storm (Krarr of the Standing Bolt).
hooks: A challenger died reaching your storm-territory and their pride blames you
The Storm has begun to hunt you as a rival
Your ridgeline territory is being taken by a rising storm-cult

ln-ancienttiger.homeland: The lost first-territories of the oldest Wilds
ln-ancienttiger.culture: Ancient Tigers claim descent from the First Age's great hunters, the oldest tigerkin bloodlines, keepers of territory-shrines older than any kingdom. Legend says their line returns in a time of breaking, and the eldest carry memory that predates the Sundering.
ln-ancienttiger.tradition: The First Claiming, a pilgrimage to a lost ancestral territory-shrine of the First Age.
ln-ancienttiger.appearance: Deep-hued ancient striping, gold-flecked eyes, first-age relic-sigils.
ln-ancienttiger.naming: A single archaic name plus an elder-territory (Ashkar of the First Grove).
rivals: Those who defile the old shrines
ln-ancienttiger.landmark: The First Grove, said to exist for those who deserve to find it
hooks: Your line is said to return only when the world is breaking, and it is stirring
An ancestral shrine you guard has been defiled
You found a First Age relic that remembers you

ln-brownbear.homeland: The forest-holds of the Emerald Wilds
ln-brownbear.culture: Brown Bears are the forest-guardian bearkin, hearth-keepers who protect the frontier-holds and Wilds villages. Slow to anger and impossible to move, they hibernate through the hardest season and wake as the fiercest defenders a community could ask for.
ln-brownbear.tradition: The First Winter, a young bearkin's first solitary hibernation-vigil, marking adulthood.
ln-brownbear.appearance: Broad, brown-furred, hearth-marked, heavy protective wraps.
ln-brownbear.naming: Given name plus a hold-name (Bruin of Green Hollow).
ln-brownbear.landmark: The frontier holds of the Wilds' edge
hooks: You woke early from the First Winter to find your hold gone
The Hunt is bearing down on the village you guard
Someone you are hearth-sworn to protect has vanished

ln-polarbear.homeland: The ice-holds of the Frostbound North
ln-polarbear.culture: Polar Bears are the ice-guardian bearkin of the far north, the mightiest of their kind, who hold the frozen holds against the Winter Hunt and the ice-reavers. They wake from the long sleep as living bulwarks, and a Polar Bear at a doorway is a wall no army passes.
ln-polarbear.tradition: The Ice-Vigil, a hibernation held in a glacier-den, waking only when the hold has need.
ln-polarbear.naming: Given name plus an ice-hold (Isbjorn of Whitehall).
ln-polarbear.landmark: Whitehall, the hall carved inside a living glacier
hooks: The Winter Hunt is at the gates of the hold you guard
You woke from the Ice-Vigil to a hold under siege
Something in the glacier is waking alongside you

ln-blackbear.homeland: The hill-country and frontier towns of the Crownlands
ln-blackbear.culture: Black Bears are the hill-and-frontier bearkin, quieter and more solitary than their cousins, who guard small communities and mind their own dens. They are the beloved protectors of many a Crownlands town, gruff but gentle until roused.
ln-blackbear.tradition: The Den-Keeping, an oath a young Black Bear swears to protect one place or family for life.
ln-blackbear.appearance: Black-furred, compact, den-marked, plain sturdy wraps.
ln-blackbear.naming: Given name plus a den or town (Cuth of Ashford).
ln-blackbear.landmark: The frontier towns of the Crownlands
hooks: The family you den-swore to protect is in danger far away
Bandits have driven you from your den
A lord means to seize the town you guard

ln-cavebear.homeland: The deep cave-holds of the Ironspine
ln-cavebear.environment: Mountain caves and the upper Blackdeep
ln-cavebear.culture: Cave Bears withdrew into the Ironspine's caves during the Age of Ash, bearkin who guard the thresholds between surface and Deep. They keep the longest hibernations of all, and a woken Cave Bear is a rare and serious omen, for they wake only for grave need.
ln-cavebear.tradition: The Deep-Sleep, a hibernation lasting years, kept at a threshold to the Deep.
ln-cavebear.appearance: Huge, dark-furred, cave-pale eyes, stone-marked wraps.
ln-cavebear.naming: Given name plus a deep-hold (Grommash of the Ninth Cave).
rivals: Whatever comes up from the Deep
hooks: You woke from the Deep-Sleep because something is coming up
The threshold you guard has been breached
A Cave Bear waking is an omen and everyone wants to know what it means

ln-greatbear.homeland: The oldest ancestor-holds of the north
ln-greatbear.culture: Great Bears are the eldest bearkin bloodline, said to descend from a Great Bear who slept a hundred years and woke to save a dying hold. Their line wakes, legend holds, only when the world itself is breaking, and the north watches their slumber for signs.
ln-greatbear.tradition: The Century-Sleep, the longest hibernation, undertaken by an elder to be ready for a great need.
ln-greatbear.naming: Given name plus an ancestor-hold (Ursaka of the First Hearth).
rivals: Those who would wake them for gain
ln-greatbear.landmark: The ancestor-shrines of the deep north
hooks: Your bloodline wakes only when the world breaks, and you have woken
An elder Great Bear is stirring and the north wants to know why
You carry the ancestor-relic of the First Hearth

ln-sunlion.homeland: The Sun Court seat of Sunspire
ln-sunlion.environment: The golden desert and sun-warmed courts
ln-sunlion.culture: Sun Lions are the desert-court lionkin, the proudest prides of the Sunscorch, who hold the sun as the source of rightful rule. Their courts run on loyalty and oratory, and a Sun Lion measures worth by the pride they lift and the pride that lifts them.
ln-sunlion.tradition: The Sun-Rite, a coming-of-age at the summer solstice, when a young lionkin swears the Pride-Oath.
ln-sunlion.appearance: Golden-maned, sun-bronzed, sun-gold ornaments, rank-braided manes.
ln-sunlion.naming: A proud name plus a court (Rasha of the Sun Court).
ln-sunlion.landmark: Sunspire, the mile-high needle that casts no shadow at noon
hooks: The Sun Court's heir is lost in the deep dunes and your pride is blamed
You are pride-less and seek a court to call your own
The Spire has begun to glow and the court is divided over the omen

ln-desertlion.homeland: The deep-dune prides of the Sunscorch
ln-desertlion.environment: The killing deep dunes far from any oasis
ln-desertlion.culture: Desert Lions are the deep-dune prides who live where the Sun Court will not go, hardier and wilder than the courtly Sun Lions. They keep the oasis-roads open and the buried cities secret, and their loyalty is to the pride and the road, not to any throne.
ln-desertlion.tradition: The Deep Crossing, a rite of surviving the deep dunes and returning with word of what the sand has uncovered.
ln-desertlion.naming: A name plus a dune-road (Karim of the Long Dune).
hooks: A storm uncovered a city your pride is sworn to keep hidden
The Sun Court demands tribute your pride cannot pay
Your Deep Crossing found something that followed you back

ln-mountainlion.homeland: The high-pass prides of the Ironspine
ln-mountainlion.environment: Mountain crags, high passes, and cliff-country
ln-mountainlion.culture: Mountain Lions are the highland prides who took to the peaks, solitary-leaning lionkin who guard the high passes and keep smaller, tighter prides than their desert kin. Agile and proud, they are the wardens of routes the caravans depend on.
ln-mountainlion.tradition: The Crag-Claiming, a rite of holding a high pass alone to earn a place in the pride.
ln-mountainlion.appearance: Grey-tawny, lean, crag-marked, mountain-wraps and claw-tokens.
ln-mountainlion.naming: A name plus a pass (Vira of the Grey Pass).
ln-mountainlion.landmark: The high passes of the Ironspine
hooks: The pass your pride guards has become a war-road
A vault-claim dispute threatens your crag-territory
Your pride's high pass is being taken by raiders

ln-goldenlion.homeland: The old royal seats of the buried desert empires
ln-goldenlion.environment: The desert and the ruins of lost sun-kingdoms
ln-goldenlion.culture: Golden Lions are the royal bloodline, lionkin who claim descent from the buried desert empires and carry crown-claims to thrones that no longer exist. Regal and burdened by legacy, they seek to restore a glory the sand swallowed, or to finally lay it to rest.
ln-goldenlion.tradition: The Crown-Reckoning, where a Golden Lion learns the true, fallen history of their line's lost throne.
ln-goldenlion.appearance: Radiant golden manes, royal bearing, ancient regalia, sun-crown marks.
ln-goldenlion.naming: A royal name plus a fallen dynasty (Aurelion of the Drowned Sun).
ln-goldenlion.landmark: The buried royal tombs of the Sunscorch
hooks: A buried empire's crown has surfaced and your bloodline is named
Your crown-claim makes you a target for those who fear a restored throne
The truth of your line's fall is worse than the legend

ln-dusklion.homeland: The shadow-border prides near the Vale
ln-dusklion.culture: Dusk Lions are the shadow-border prides, lionkin who hold the failing light at the world's edge, prouder for standing where others flee. Marked by the endless dusk, they keep court in the gloom and defend the last lit lands against the advancing dark.
ln-dusklion.tradition: The Dusk-Oath, a Pride-Oath sworn to hold the border where the light thins.
ln-dusklion.appearance: Dusk-tawny with shadowed manes, dim-gold eyes, border-wraps.
ln-dusklion.naming: A name plus a dusk-hold (Sekh of the Last Light).
hooks: The border-light is failing and your pride's oath with it
Refugees flee the dark into your pride's lands
The Unlit mean to snuff the last light your pride guards
